title: Which tool has good vector style asset generation? I see a lot for pixel art and 3D for characters, but I'm looking for something that could generate, for example, a vector art-style fountain with running water, as a spritesheet.
author: CelestialButterflies
selftext:
I am making a lot of my assets by hand in Inkscape with simple shapes, just to say that I did lol. But I want to use AI to help me with animations. Whenever I search for AI animation tools, they all highlight pixel art or 3D characters. Which is great, but I'm looking more toward objects. Ideally it would export to a spritesheet so I could trace it or something in Inkscape, but even cooler if it could export directly to SVG. Bonus BONUS points if it could use a premade color palette too.

Thanks for the help!

comments.author: macuseri686
comments.body:
interesting question. i feel like the reason that the AI may be leading you astray is because you are asking specifically about spritesheets. by definition, a spritesheet is a bitmapped frame-by-frame animation. a vector graphic like an SVG uses vector shapes declared using XML to draw mathematical shapes at any scale. SVG also natively supports transformative animation. So to create an SVG animation, is much different than creating a spritesheet. you simply setup a bunch of timed transforms for each of the different shapes and points of the SVG in the actual XML file.

that being said, if you are interested in spritesheets, I run the Gamelabs Studio spritesheet animation platform.

replies.author: CelestialButterflies
replies.body:
Thanks! I have actually used Codex to animate SVG files before, for a kanji game I was making. It's pretty neat, but not really what I am looking for. 

It'd be cool if the initial image generation could output SVG. Illustrator's AI can do it but it is not good lol. The SVG file would allow me to swap colors and edit shapes as I need to.

 As for spritesheets, you're right. I didn't think about that. So I guess i wouldn't ask for the spritesheet to be an SVG... I'd want multiple SVGs that could be organized into a spritesheet. All the same picture but for each frame. Only need 3 or 4 frames for my purposes.

My art is all vectors but the game engine still needs them as pngs. Vectors are just easier to make stuff with, imo.

Right now, I am generating the animated sheet with Ludo and tracing it in Inkscape (tho there's also the Trace Bitmap, it doesn't work right for me lol). This works fine for now!

replies.author: macuseri686
replies.body:
technically, i guess you could take each of the frames from the bitmapped spritesheet animation and convert them to SVG using something like this: [https://www.adobe.com/express/feature/image/convert/svg](https://www.adobe.com/express/feature/image/convert/svg)

its just trying to approximate the SVG paths though, based on rounding the bitmapped pixels

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: All the existing AI animation generators that use spritesheet format do so by doing img -> vid and then cutting out select frames from the video to use in the sheet. So you're not going to find these outputting svg formats. I personally use Spine 2D, but you're not going to get an AI to help you with that. It does allow for layering thoug. Do note that if your goal is just to change colors of things, you can do color range swaps in engines like Godot, at runtime, in order to change something like water color, as long as that color you're working with is a flat color or fairly concise set of colors that can all be grabbed with in the range you choose.

comments.author: Aesthetic-Engine
comments.body:
Godot + Godot Runtime Bridge + Cursor/Claude Code/Codex. 

You just prompt your coding tool what you want it to generate and export. Given direct access to Godot all the major AI coding tools can build vector art very well as it's all math and lines.
